precepts.text: Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the Lord understand all things. That is why some are always confused when leadership passes a judgment: they do not know the scriptures, so they do not understand the sentence of judgment.
precepts.point: This chapter deals with the man whose whole occupation is his worldly craft. Without these cannot a city be inhabited; the work is needed. But they shall not be sought for in public counsel, nor sit high in the congregation, nor sit on the judges' seat, nor understand the sentence of judgment. If all you know is your job and not the scriptures, why would you be asked anything in counsel?
precepts.why:
Sirach says the man whose whole occupation is his worldly job shall not “understand the sentence of judgment”. Why don't you understand when judgments are passed? Proverbs answers: “Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the Lord understand all things.”

That is the brother who is always confused. When leadership makes a judgment, he doesn't agree, even if he disagrees in silence. You don't agree because you don't know the scriptures. All you know is your job, not the word of God, so you are always confused. And the Bible says you are evil.

So that brother “shall not be sought for in publick counsel”. When things are going down, we don't want to hear your opinion, because your opinion is your work, your job. He will not “sit high in the congregation” or have rank, and he will not “be found where parables are spoken”, because he could care less. If the shoe fits, brother, wear it. If you want to be a member, be a member; there is nothing wrong with that.

But they that seek the Lord understand all things. Chapter 39 shows the flip side: the one that “giveth his mind to the law of the most High”. He seeks out the wisdom of the ancients, is found where the subtle parables are, and he shall serve among great men and appear before princes.

precepts.text: Weep bitterly a day or two for the dead, then comfort thyself for thy heaviness, for of heaviness cometh death and the heaviness of the heart breaketh strength. Stress makes a man weak: you do not want to work out, you eat more, you gain weight, and eventually it is death. Brothers, do not let stress keep you from the work; some of you have sat in regular clothes for years with the prophecies coming to pass. What is keeping you back is sin. Examine yourself. The Most High is doing his part; it is time we do ours.
precepts.point: Love thine own soul, comfort thy heart, and remove sorrow far from thee, for sorrow hath killed many. Captain Shamai has pushed working out for five years; a brother lost serious weight only by changing his diet and walking an hour a day around his neighborhood. Walk before you go in the house after a twelve-hour shift, because once you are inside you have more excuses than a crackhead.
precepts.why:
“Give not over thy mind to heaviness.” Every class is preparing you for what is coming: rent, mortgage, food and gas are going sky-high, ten dollars a gallon, and you will not get a raise. Can you change it? Then why worry about it? “Love thine own soul, and comfort thy heart, remove sorrow far from thee: for sorrow hath killed many.” Stress and worry have killed many, and you are no different.

Sirach shows what heaviness does: “Weep bitterly, and make great moan, and use lamentation, as he is worthy, and that a day or two, lest thou be evil spoken of: and then comfort thyself for thy heaviness.” This is speaking of when somebody passes: mourn, and then comfort yourself.

“For of heaviness cometh death, and the heaviness of the heart breaketh strength.” Heaviness, stress, brings death. And the heaviness of the heart breaks strength: stress makes a man weak. When you are stressed, you don’t want to work out, you don’t want to go to work. Some people eat more; you gain weight, you become fat and sloppy, you lay back, and eventually it is death.

So, brothers, do not let stress wear you down so that you don’t want to do the Most High’s work. Some of you have sat here five or six years in regular clothes. You see the prophecies coming to pass, wars all over the place, World War III a matter of time, and you still sit there. What are you waiting for? What is keeping you back is sin. Examine yourself.

When correction comes, push harder; prove to Messiah you are still in the fight. Don’t hold grudges and keep to yourself, because that is when Satan messes with your head. A merry heart makes a cheerful countenance, but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken. The Most High is doing his part. It is time we do ours.

precepts.text: He that sinneth before his Maker, let him fall into the hand of the physician.
precepts.point: Calling this bullying means refusing to take heed, and that brings a short life. That is the Bible's word, not the teacher's.
precepts.why:
“For excess of meats bringeth sickness, and surfeiting will turn into choler.” That belly ache late at night, that belly pain: you are sick. “By surfeiting have many perished; but he that taketh heed prolongeth his life.” The Bible says if you keep overeating, you are going to die. So I guess the Bible is a bully’s book? No. You just hate God and you hate yourself, because loving God is the only way to love yourself. When the white man’s own Department of Health says eight Swedish fish is past a child’s safe arsenic level, you say nothing; when we tell you to stop eating junk, it’s bullying. If you call it bullying, you will not take heed, and you will live a very short life. That is what the Bible says, not what I say.

Then Sirach says: “He that sinneth before his Maker, let him fall into the hand of the physician.” What will make you get sick and fall into the hand of the physician? Overeating. The Bible says, if you want to live long, don’t do it. But do we take heed? No, we don’t.

Fat does not stay harmlessly under the skin. Visceral fat wraps around the heart, the lungs, the liver, the stomach and the intestines, and makes your organs work double time, so you always feel weak, tired, low on energy. You don’t feel pain, so you don’t think it’s happening, until one day, bam, stroke; bam, heart attack; high cholesterol, heart bypass surgery. Eating sugar and overeating, you walk around like a ticking time bomb.

That is what we are trying to prevent: you ending up in a hospital bed, in the physician’s hand, because you sinned against your Maker with your mouth. Take heed to what is written, and prolong your life.

precepts.text: Honour the physician, but healing itself comes from the Most High.
precepts.point: Asa dies in the one and fortieth year of his reign and is buried in his own sepulchre in the city of David, on a bed of sweet odours and spices, with a very great burning.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 16: Asa Leans on Syria Instead of the Most High

precepts.why:
“Honour a physician with the honour due unto him for the uses which ye may have of him: for the Lord hath created him. For of the most High cometh healing.”

Asa “was diseased in his feet, until his disease was exceeding great: yet in his disease he sought not to the Lord, but to the physicians.” The rebuke is not against physicians. The Lord created the physician, and he is to be honoured. The rebuke is against seeking them in place of the Most High, from whom healing cometh.

precepts.text: In sickness pray to the Most High and leave off from sin, then seek the physician.
precepts.point: Asa dies in the one and fortieth year of his reign and is buried in his own sepulchre in the city of David, on a bed of sweet odours and spices, with a very great burning.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 16: Asa Leans on Syria Instead of the Most High

precepts.why:
“My son, in thy sickness be not negligent: but pray unto the Lord, and he will make thee whole. Leave off from sin, and order thine hands aright, and cleanse thy heart from all wickedness.”

That is the order: in sickness pray to the Most High and leave off from sin, then seek the physician. Asa did it backwards: “in his disease he sought not to the Lord, but to the physicians.” And “Asa slept with his fathers, and died in the one and fortieth year of his reign.”

“For of heaviness cometh death”. Heaviness is depression and distress, and it can cause you to die: internal organ failure, and thoughts of suicide. Brothers have thoughts of suicide because they let the depression get to them.

“And the heaviness of the heart breaketh strength.” It makes you weak. It makes you not want to eat, not want to congregate, not want to come around the brothers anymore. That is why Ecclesiasticus 30:21 says, give not over thy mind to heaviness. So how do we get our strength, our healing, our help?

note.label: Do You Know What Happened To Rasheem Carter?

precepts.why:
This is the scripture I left out when I brought up the death of the Israelite leader last week, and it’s for you Black Hebrew Israelites with hatred in your heart, ready to attack a man you don’t know nothing about, who just jumped on a rumor when you saw the white man come out and start doing videos.

“When the dead is at rest”: when someone dies they’re in a state of rest. “Let his remembrance rest”: don’t start disrespecting that man. “And be comforted for him, when his Spirit is departed from him.” That’s a law, and it’s not kept in the Black Hebrew Israelite community; you men are ungodly. That is the gain of oppression Isaiah 33:15 says the righteous man despiseth.

“The wisdom of a learned man cometh by opportunity of leisure”: you got to take your time and get in this Bible, because there’s a lot of nuggets in here, a lot of things you could figure out to help you navigate through this evil world. A lot of you are not taking the opportunity of leisure to just sit down and learn God and watch class. You have something the generations before you never had: to just sit in a place and learn and soak it up like a sponge.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
This is for you brothers who put your job ahead of God’s work. “They shall not be sought for in publick counsel, nor sit high in the congregation”: don’t look for rank if your job is your first priority.

“They shall not sit on the judges’ seat, nor understand the sentence of judgment”: don’t ask why you don’t understand certain judgments. You’ve not been around, you’ve not studied, you’ve not prayed nor applied, but you’ve gone to work sun up to sundown every day. “They cannot declare justice and judgment; and they shall not be found where parables are spoken”: when we’re going over parables you’re nowhere around.

“But they will maintain the state of the world”: your whole life is maintaining the United States of America. “And all their desire is in the work of their craft.”

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

precepts.why:
“The wisdom of a learned man cometh by opportunity of leisure: and he that hath little business shall become wise.” To give yourself wholly you have to prioritize what is really important to you. When brothers are exhorted they rattle off the list of all their responsibilities in the world. Nobody cares: not insensitively, but those excuses are lies.

It does not mean you do one and not the other; you can do both. “How can he get wisdom that holdeth the plough, and that glorieth in the goad, that driveth oxen, and is occupied in their labours, and whose talk is of bullocks?” Unless you make the effort to give yourself to this. When all you talk about is everything else in your life, you are saying loudly, I’m not really about this yet.

You want to be part of this on your time, your conditions and your schedule. Nobody is told to quit their job; find a way. Where your treasure is, there your heart is, and this has not become your treasure yet. You are not ready to spend and be spent.

A sweet savour and a memorial of fine flour, meaning a sacrifice. We no longer give this memorial of a sacrifice of fine flour, because Christ took the place of the sacrifice. So now we as a people must pray to the heavenly father in the name of Christ.
Once you've prayed to the Lord, you've sacrificed the words of your lips in the name of Christ, then give place to the physician. Don't let him go from thee: you got need of a doctor.
The physician back in the ancient days used to pray unto the Lord that he would prosper that which they give for ease and remedy, to prolong life.

He that sinneth before his maker, he that breaks the commandments, let him fall into the hand of the physician: you better go to the doctor, because you are about to get jacked up in the body. You're about to get sick, you're about to catch a disease.

Heaviness, meaning depression, sorrow, comes death. When you are so sorrowful over some incident you're going through in your life, it can break your spirit. Once your spirit is broken it brings forth disease, and once that disease takes over it brings forth death. There is a cause and effect: sorrow can lead to sickness and disease also; the Most High allows that.

Take no sorrow to your mind. You see something that's about to make you sorrowful: drive it away, because that sorrow, once it takes hold in you, it can take hold so hard you can't come out of that state of depression, and it's going to lead to sickness and disease and ultimately death.
Remember the last end is death, if you take hold on that sorrow.

The one that died that you crying for: you crying and crying, you can't do that man or that woman, your child, your mother, your father any good. You going to hurt yourself, because he or she is already dead; the baby's dead already. If you sorrow too much you going to hurt yourself.
I can't skip it, cuz some of us have this mindset.

You go to work every day. You try to get around your supervisor, your foreman, to better your position so you can better the situation that you have at home, which is fine. Make your money. points: They shall not be sought for in publick counsel: the men that's underneath you notice. Maybe they came to you before and you shunned them away, or you didn't have the answers. It's fine if you don't have the answers, but make sure that you get the answers and come back with it, so they can see that you are apt to teach. But when they see that you only about maintaining the state of the world and about your craft, don't think the congregation don't see that.
Ain't nobody coming up to you for no questions. They don't care about your answers cuz they know you probably don't got it. Trust me, the congregation know when you're not studying.

Nor sit high in the congregation: they shall not sit on the judges' seat, because you didn't build your spirit up enough to even be amongst the judges. Nor understand the sentence of judgment: because you didn't take it seriously. When you maintain the state of the world, the congregation is not going to look for you to teach them, and you start losing the love of the people.

points: The wisdom of a learned man cometh by opportunity of leisure: being addicted to the scriptures and the understanding of God's word comes from an opportunity of leisure.

And he that hath little business shall become wise: you got to get off of social media. You got to stop working so damn much. You might work to take care of your family, I get it, but you have to sit down and force yourself to do the work of the Lord, to be addicted to seeking the wisdom in God's law.

note.label: Social Media - Weapons of Mass Distraction

points: The first thing that we want to look out for is somebody that's always talking about money or work.
How can he get wisdom that holdeth the plough: so the Bible says there's going to be a conflict. You're trying to get wisdom, but you always at work.
And that glorieth in the goad: not only do you always be at work, but you glory in that thing. Your mind is always wrapped around the job.
And is occupied in their labours: your profession is your job. Your occupation is your job, but our occupation is the word of the Most High. Going to the blitzes, waking up the 12 tribes of Israel.
And whose talk is of bullocks: whose conversation is always about work, it's always about money.

The Bible says that these type of men will not sit in the judge's seat. Not only will they not sit in the judge's seat, the scripture says they won't even understand judgment. They always talking about money, they always talking about work. The Lord says they not going to have the spirit of wisdom on them.
Nor sit high in the congregation: they won't be leaders amongst the nation.
And they shall not be found where parables are spoken: they're not going to be around the leadership either. Why? They was at work.

This is the type of brother or sister that when the job calls and says, hey, Mr. Such and such or Mrs. Such and such, we need you to come in on Saturday this week, they're going to look to the left, they're going to look to the right, and they're going to say, yes sir, boss, I'll be there.

So these people who glorify their job, they glorify money, they will be willing to compromise for the right dollar amount. They will betray you if the price is right. They're subtly telling you, by always talking about money, always talking about their job, that they have a price where they can be bought. They will betray Christ. They will betray the laws of God. They will break the Sabbath, and they will betray you too.

That brother or sister that says, well, I got to do what I got to do to provide for my family: what's the difference between them and the drug dealer? Don't drug dealers say the same thing? Can you trust a drug dealer? No. So you can't trust a brother or sister that will idolize their money above the laws of God.

This is still letting bad situations destroy you. “For of heaviness cometh death”: that heaviness is depression. Of depression comes death; death is coming. “And the heaviness of the heart breaketh strength”: the heaviness of the heart is the depression of the mind, and it breaks your spiritual strength, which leads to your physical breaking. Sometimes we go through health issues, and that man or that woman refuses to try to increase their physical strength and their spiritual strength.

“In affliction also sorrow remaineth”: when you are afflicted, sorrow remains, like the brother and the sister we saw in California; their sorrow is going to remain for quite a while, till their situation is fixed. “And the life of the poor is the curse of the heart”: being poor will make you rob, steal and kill.
As we go through these scriptures, apply them to yourself. Don't think this class isn't pertaining to you. This class is for you.

“Take no heaviness to heart”: these bad situations happen; do not take them to heart. “Drive it away”: when you have that spirit of depression and sorrow, God says drive it away. “And member the last end”: remember the end, because sorrow will break bones. It will break you.
